note: Hard-coded Korean string literals left per client (area of scripts/check-locales.js). The count must equal its area's budget: more is a new literal, fewer means the budget is stale; lower it with node scripts/check-locales.js --write-budget, which never raises one. Stage 2-1 added a last-resort count of Hangul the literal pattern cannot see (inside interpolations and Swift/C# """ blocks), so the other areas were re-based on that true count: macOS core 872→874, WinUI 189→190, phone 202→219; Windows Core fell 161→137 when SlashCommandStrings moved to the shared keys macOS reads. Exemptions and allowed literals are not counted; each says why, and one that no longer matches anything fails the check.
